The platform's log shows the in-app notice was sent at 12:01:40, twenty seconds before the 12:02:00 start, so the notice reached the rider before the point of pickup [F9].

The notice text reads: “Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $29.75. You can cancel for free.” [F9]. That states the new multiplier (1.4×), states a revised estimated fare ($29.75), and states expressly that the rider can cancel for free — all three items SURGE-1 requires [SURGE-1]. I read the words in context, not by keyword: the revised fare is a stated estimate, and an estimate that differs from the finally charged fare ($27.82) is still a stated estimate [F5][F9]. The notice therefore satisfies SURGE-1: [SURGE-1:notice] is met, and the consequence the trace fixes for that reading is that the higher fare stands [SURGE-2].

The rider's complaint that the notice "only popped up as I was getting into the car, I had no real chance to cancel" is a statement; the in-app log is a system record of when the message was sent — before the trip start — and system records override statements where they conflict [F9][SURGE-1]. The rider's complaint also does not contradict the notice's content, which expressly offered penalty-free cancellation [F9][SURGE-2].
